lede: The biggest item this week is Mountain Village Town Council taking up a resolution to set the sale price appreciation cap on deed-restricted units — the fine print that decides whether affordable housing actually stays affordable for the next buyer, not just the first one. Council also considers a 2026 budget appropriation amendment. Meanwhile, Telluride's Planning and Zoning Commission holds a public hearing and a first look at the school district's employee housing proposal for the middle-high school site on West Colorado.

notable.stake: Vote on appreciation cap determines if deed-restricted units stay genuinely affordable long-term.
